name: ARA-290

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Rodent nerve-pain, kidney and diabetes models

track.title: Phase II
track.line: Phase 2 trials in sarcoidosis and diabetes, Araim

what.text: ARA-290 (international name cibinetide) is a chain of 11 amino acids, pyroglutamate-Glu-Gln-Leu-Glu-Arg-Ala-Leu-Asn-Ser-Ser. It was designed from part of erythropoietin (EPO), the hormone that makes the body produce red blood cells, but it does not raise red blood cell production.

what.text: Its developer, Araim Pharmaceuticals, describes it as acting on the “innate repair receptor,” a receptor that animal studies link to tissue protection and lower inflammation after injury. Araim officers who own stock in the company co-wrote several of the trials below.

src.label: Culver DA, et al. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2017
Lois N, et al. J Clin Med 2020
Brines M, et al. Mol Med 2015, full text

what.text: ARA-290 has been tested in a few small trials for nerve pain. It is not approved anywhere.

research.text: ARA-290 has been tested in people in a handful of small trials, mostly in people with sarcoidosis or type 2 diabetes who had small-fiber nerve damage and pain. Araim ran or co-wrote several of them. No trial has tested it for muscle or sports injuries, and no Phase 3 trial has been run.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Sarcoidosis with small-fiber neuropathy, IV doses, 2012

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled exploratory trial
22 people with sarcoidosis, nerve symptoms and a pain score of 5 or more (12 on ARA-290, 10 on placebo)
ARA-290 2 mg or placebo into a vein three times a week
4 weeks
pain, a small-fiber neuropathy symptom score, quality of life, depression and fatigue

research.found: The neuropathy symptom score improved more with ARA-290 than placebo at week 4. Pain and fatigue scores improved equally in both groups. No safety concerns were found.

src.label: Heij L, et al. Mol Med 2012

research.title: Sarcoidosis with small nerve fiber loss, injections under the skin, 2013

facts.v: blinded, placebo-controlled trial
38 people with sarcoidosis and documented small nerve fiber loss (18 women, 20 men; mean age 49.5)
ARA-290 or placebo by injection under the skin once a day
28 days, then 12 weeks of follow-up
nerve symptoms, corneal nerve fiber density, skin temperature sensing and a 6-minute walk test

research.found: Symptoms improved more with ARA-290, and corneal nerve fiber density rose. No serious adverse events occurred and no antibodies to ARA-290 were found. Araim staff were among the authors.

src.label: Dahan A, et al. Mol Med 2013
Dahan A, et al. Mol Med 2013, full text

research.meta: USA and Netherlands · 2014–2015 · Phase 2b randomized, placebo-controlled
research.title: Sarcoidosis nerve fiber loss, dose-ranging, Araim (NCT02039687)

facts.v: randomized, quadruple-blind; three doses (1, 4 or 8 mg a day under the skin) or placebo
64 adults with sarcoidosis-related small nerve fiber loss and nerve pain
28 days
main goal: change in corneal nerve fiber area

research.found: Only the 4 mg group had a statistically significant rise in corneal nerve fiber area. Pain improved in all groups, including placebo; the difference from placebo was not significant. Serious events included fainting and suicidal thoughts in single participants (see Side effects).

src.label: Culver DA, et al. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2017
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02039687

research.title: Type 2 diabetes with painful neuropathy, 2014

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled, investigator-initiated (Netherlands Trial Register NTR3858)
49 people with type 2 diabetes and painful feet or hands enrolled; 48 analyzed
ARA-290 4 mg or placebo, self-injected under the skin once a day
28 days, then 28 days without treatment
safety, HbA1c (long-term blood sugar), nerve pain questionnaires and corneal nerve fibers

research.found: HbA1c and one nerve pain score improved in the ARA-290 group. Corneal nerve fiber density rose in a subgroup. Four serious adverse events occurred on ARA-290; two were judged possibly related (a slight worsening of kidney function and a severe leg skin infection). Three authors were Araim officers.

src.label: Brines M, et al. Mol Med 2015
Brines M, et al. Mol Med 2015, full text

research.title: Diabetic macular edema (eye swelling), Belfast

facts.v: open-label, no control group (ISRCTN16962255; NCT06626971)
9 people with diabetes and macular edema; 8 completed
cibinetide 4 mg a day under the skin
12 weeks
visual acuity, retinal thickness and other eye measures

research.found: Vision and retinal thickness did not improve on average. A vision questionnaire score improved. No serious adverse events or antibodies were seen. The trial ended early because the study drug expired with no replacement.

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06626971

research.title: Healthy volunteers, emotion processing, 2015

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, parallel-group; one dose of ARA-290 2 mg or placebo
36 healthy adults aged 18 to 35
tested one week after the dose
brain responses to faces (MRI) and emotion tests

research.found: Some measures of emotional processing changed; mood did not.

research.text: A further Phase 2 trial in people with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes in Stockholm (NCT01933529, 24 planned) has no posted results; its status is listed as unknown.

src.label: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01933529

research.text: In a 2026 case report, three dental patients with nerve injury got ARA-290 mixed with BPC-157, TB-500 and dexamethasone. Their numbness lessened, but the report had no control group and the authors say spontaneous recovery cannot be ruled out.

src.label: Froum S, et al. Front Oral Health 2026

us.text: ARA-290 is not FDA approved for any use. It was nominated for pharmacy compounding, and FDA put it in category 3: nominated without adequate support. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. Drugs@FDA lists no approved drug containing cibinetide.

after.text: ARA-290 is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. Class S2.1.5 bans “innate repair receptor agonists, e.g. asialo EPO; carbamylated EPO,” at all times, and ARA-290’s developers describe it as an innate repair receptor agonist. Whether WADA applies S2.1.5 to ARA-290 was not confirmed. S2 substances are not “specified substances.” The 2027 list keeps S2.1.5 unchanged.

side.text: The trials were small and short. Most found no clear drug-related safety problem, but a few serious events were judged possibly related.

items.text: serious adverse events: in the 1 mg group, 2 of 16 people (fainting, headache, chest tightness, shortness of breath, small-bowel inflammation); in the 8 mg group, 1 of 14 (suicidal thoughts); none on 4 mg or placebo. Common events included headache, nausea, diarrhea, tiredness and injection-site pain, which also occurred on placebo.

src.label: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02039687

items.text: of four serious events on ARA-290, two were judged possibly related: slight worsening of kidney function in a man on a diuretic, and a severe leg skin infection (cellulitis) needing hospital care.
